working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: Most UK golfers who make the trip to County Down fly in, play Royal County Down, and fly home. This post makes the case for treating it as a proper three-course circuit, covering how to actually get a tee time at each club, what the courses are genuinely like to play, and how to string the trip together logistically.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD), Newcastle: sits between the Mourne Mountains and the Irish Sea; two courses on site: the Championship Links and the Annesley Links. Championship Links consistently ranked among the world's top courses. Founded 1889. Address: 36 Golf Links Road, Newcastle, BT33 0AN.
- RCD visitor access is restricted and tightly managed: Championship Links open to visitors on Mon, Tue, Fri (morning and afternoon), Thu (mornings) and Sun (afternoons) only. Tee sheet released once per year, typically opening around 1 April for the following season. Must call the club directly; no advance request system. Full payment required at time of booking. High-season dates fill immediately.
- RCD Championship course plays to 7,186 yards from the tips; the course is famous for blind tee shots, especially the 9th, which requires a tee shot over a dune with the fairway shifting below. Caddies strongly recommended; fees in the region of £60–£100 plus tip. Forecaddies sometimes mandatory for groups of 3–4. Walking is standard; no buggies.
- RCD green fees range from approximately £30 (Annesley) to £220 (Championship peak); exact current pricing should be confirmed directly with the club.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, established 1896, par 70, approx. 6,268 yards. Clubhouse occupies part of a fortified building dating to the 15th century (one of the oldest clubhouse buildings in the world). Irish Sea comes into play on 8 holes and is visible from all 18. Located roughly 30 minutes from RCD at Newcastle, and about 50 minutes from Belfast. Visitors welcome; restrictions apply on Saturdays and Sundays (pre-booking required). No handicap certificate required. Opening five holes hug the cliffs.
- Ardglass is frequently described as an underrated companion to RCD, offering a more accessible green fee. Widely regarded as excellent value.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: 18-hole links, established 1902, current layout revised by James Braid in 1934. Located in Cloughey on the Ards Peninsula. Par 70, approx. 6,167 yards (Medal). Most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland. Nearest links course to Belfast (approx. 45 minutes by road). Free-draining sandy base means course is rarely closed, even after heavy rain — a genuine year-round option. Visitors welcome. Signature hole: par-4 10th, reputedly one of the toughest par 4s in Irish golf. Elevated tees and greens are a feature. Recently recognised as 'Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster'. On-site: Charlie's Bar and Bistro, pro shop, practice facilities.
- Getting there from mainland UK: fly to Belfast City Airport (BHD, approx. 30–40 minutes to Newcastle/Downpatrick by car) or Belfast International (BFS, approx. 1 hour to Newcastle). Multiple UK airports served including London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Bristol, Liverpool. Ferry options: P&O Irish Sea and Stena Line from Cairnryan/Stranraer to Larne or Belfast — useful if bringing own car with clubs.
- Driving within County Down: a car is essentially required to do the three-course circuit. Newcastle (RCD) is approx. 45 minutes from Belfast via the A24. Ardglass is approx. 30 minutes from Newcastle. Kirkistown is on the Ards Peninsula, approx. 45 minutes from Belfast.
- Accommodation: Slieve Donard Resort and Spa is adjacent to RCD in Newcastle and is the obvious base for the championship course. The Burrendale Hotel in Newcastle is a less expensive nearby alternative. Belfast (50+ minutes from Newcastle) widens accommodation options considerably for those on a budget.
- A logical three-day circuit: Day 1 Kirkistown (year-round, accessible, easy booking), Day 2 Ardglass (clifftop drama, great value), Day 3 RCD Championship (the bucket-list closer). Alternatively Annesley Links at RCD can substitute if Championship tee times are unavailable.

- Do not invent or attribute quotes to any golfer, pro, reviewer, or club official.
- Do not claim personal first-hand experience of any of these courses.
- No gambling or betting content (e.g. no reference to golf betting markets).
- No medical or injury advice beyond generic warm-up guidance.
- No financial advice on affordability; describe costs factually if mentioned at all.
- RCD tee-time booking rules are strict and change; direct readers to contact the club directly rather than stating any booking process as definitive.
